intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit
experiences.description: A manageable 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside a volcanic crater offering panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Best tackled at sunrise to beat the heat and crowds. Kids ages 5 and up can typically complete this trail, making it a memorable family achievement.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 11:20 AM — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, collect baggage and arrange ground transportation to your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park. Note: The listed accommodation is in Buena Park, CA — if this is a layover or staging point before Hawaii, use the afternoon to rest, freshen up, and explore the immediate Orangethorpe Ave area on foot. Visit a nearby grocery store (Walmart or Stater Bros) to stock up on snacks and essentials for the trip ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to Downtown Disney or the Anaheim GardenWalk (both within a short drive/rideshare) for a free evening walk. Window-shop and enjoy the atmosphere without spending on park tickets.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing — look for grab-and-go options under $10.
meals.lunch: In-N-Out Burger on nearby Beach Blvd (~$8–10 per person) — a California classic and very budget-friendly.
meals.dinner: Panda Express or Raising Cane's near Buena Park (~$10–12 per person) — quick, filling, and easy after a travel day.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is primarily a travel and recovery day. Confirm onward flights or inter-island arrangements to Hawaii if this stop is a connection. Keep spending minimal — big adventures start tomorrow or once you reach the islands.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for Honolulu (or your chosen Hawaiian island). If flying from LAX or John Wayne Airport, aim for a morning departure. Upon arrival in Hawaii, check in to your budget accommodation (look for hostels like Polynesian Hostel Beach Club ~$35–50/night or budget Airbnbs in Waikiki). Drop bags and head straight to Waikiki Beach — it's free and just steps from most budget lodging.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Waikiki Beach on foot. Swim, relax, and soak in your first Hawaiian afternoon. Walk the Kalakaua Avenue strip to get your bearings. Visit Kapiolani Park (free) at the east end of Waikiki — great for families with open lawns and shade trees.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the Duke Kahanamoku Statue on the beach for a classic Hawaii photo. Watch the free hula and live music performances at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (free shows most evenings around 6:30 PM).

meals.breakfast: Airport grab-and-go or convenience store near hotel (~$5–8).
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In on Kapahulu Ave — a legendary local plate lunch spot. Loco moco or mixed plate ~$10–13.
meals.dinner: Musubi Cafe Iyasume near Waikiki — spam musubi, onigiri, and bento boxes for $8–12. Perfect budget Hawaiian dinner.

day_by_day.notes: August in Hawaii averages highs around 85–88°F (29–31°C) — much warmer than the 16.8°C listed, which may reflect a different location. Pack reef-safe sunscreen. Rain showers are brief and common; carry a light poncho.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit — start early (6:00–7:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. This 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside a volcanic crater offers stunning panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Entry fee is $5/person (walk-in). Bring water and wear good shoes. Kids 5+ can manage this hike comfortably.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, cool off at nearby Kaimana Beach (Sans Souci Beach) — less crowded than Waikiki, calm waters, great for families. Free parking and entry. Bring a picnic lunch from a nearby store.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Waikiki. Browse the International Market Place outdoor mall (free to walk through). Catch the sunset from the beach around 7:00 PM.

meals.breakfast: Grab malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from Leonard's Bakery on Kapahulu Ave — 2 for ~$3. A must-try Hawaii treat.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic: grab sandwiches, fruit, and drinks from Times Supermarket or Foodland (~$8–10 per person).
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood on Kapahulu Ave — fresh poke bowls for ~$12–15. One of Oahu's best budget poke spots.

day_by_day.notes: Book Diamond Head entry online in advance at gostateparks.hawaii.gov to guarantee your spot — timed entry reservations are required. Morning slots fill fast in August.

day_by_day.morning: Take TheBus (Oahu's public transit, $3/ride or $7.50 day pass) to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — one of Hawaii's best snorkeling spots. Entry is $25/adult, free for kids under 13. Arrive early (opens 6:45 AM) as entry is capped. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then snorkel among hundreds of tropical fish in a protected bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, take TheBus along the scenic Kalanianaole Highway to Makapuu Beach Park — a beautiful bodysurfing beach with dramatic cliffs. Free entry. Families can enjoy the views and tide pools even if the surf is too strong for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki via bus. Relax and shower. Walk to Kalakaua Avenue for evening people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (Spam musubi + juice) from ABC Stores in Waikiki ~$5–7.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and sandwiches from a grocery store to eat at Hanauma Bay's picnic area — no outside food allowed inside the preserve, but you can eat at the top before descending.
meals.dinner: Marugame Udon in Waikiki — fresh udon noodles starting at $6, tempura add-ons for $1–2 each. Excellent budget family dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay is closed on Tuesdays — if this falls on a Tuesday, swap Day 4 and Day 5 activities. Snorkel gear can be rented at Hanauma Bay for ~$12. Reef-safe sunscreen is mandatory.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — take TheBus to the Arizona Memorial. The USS Arizona Memorial boat tour is FREE (first-come, first-served tickets; arrive by 7:00 AM). The outdoor grounds, memorials, and museum exhibits are also free. This is a deeply moving and educational experience for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free outdoor exhibits at Pearl Harbor including the USS Oklahoma Memorial and the Road to War museum galleries. If budget allows, the USS Bowfin Submarine Museum is $27/adult, $10/child — optional but fascinating for kids.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Aloha Tower Marketplace on the Honolulu waterfront (free to explore). Enjoy harbor views and browse local shops.

meals.breakfast: Liliha Bakery near downtown Honolulu — famous for coco puffs and pancakes. Breakfast ~$10–13 per person.
meals.lunch: Zippy's Restaurant near Pearl Harbor — a beloved local chain. Chili rice or saimin noodle soup ~$9–12.
meals.dinner: Highway Inn Kaka'ako — authentic Hawaiian plate lunch (kalua pig, poi, laulau). Dinner plates ~$14–16. A true taste of local culture.

day_by_day.notes: Free Arizona Memorial tickets are distributed on a first-come basis starting at 7:00 AM. Arrive very early in August as demand is high. No bags larger than a small purse allowed inside the memorial.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take TheBus to the North Shore of Oahu — about 1 hour from Waikiki. Visit Waimea Bay Beach Park (free) — a stunning crescent beach with calm summer waters perfect for swimming and snorkeling. In August, the bay is typically calm and safe for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along Kamehameha Highway to Sunset Beach and Ehukai Beach Park (Banzai Pipeline) — walk the beach, explore tide pools, and enjoy the scenery. Stop at Matsumoto Shave Ice in Haleiwa town — a legendary North Shore institution.
day_by_day.evening: Browse the charming surf town of Haleiwa — free to walk around. Visit local art galleries and surf shops. Head back to Waikiki before dark.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Waikiki before departing — convenience store items or a quick cafe (~$6–9).
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck parked near Kahuku — famous garlic shrimp plates for ~$14–16. A North Shore bucket-list meal.
meals.dinner: Matsumoto Shave Ice for a sweet treat (~$4–6), then a simple dinner back in Waikiki at Marugame Udon or a grocery store deli (~$8–10).

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore drive is beautiful but can have traffic. Consider renting a car for this day (~$40–60/day from budget rental companies like Dollar or Thrifty) for maximum flexibility. Gas up before leaving Honolulu.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum (Hawaii's premier natural history and cultural museum) — adult tickets ~$25, children ~$17. Spend the morning exploring Hawaiian cultural artifacts, a real Hawaiian royal palace hall, and the Science Adventure Center. Great for families with kids of all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ala Moana Beach Park (free) — a beautiful, calm beach adjacent to the massive Ala Moana Center mall. The beach has lifeguards, restrooms, and picnic areas. Perfect for a relaxed family afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through Ala Moana Center (free) — Hawaii's largest open-air mall. Browse local stores and enjoy the free Friday evening hula show at the mall's center stage (check schedule at alamoanacenter.com).

meals.breakfast: Cafe 100 in Hilo-style (or similar local diner near hotel) — loco moco breakfast ~$9–11.
meals.lunch: Ala Moana Center Food Court — wide variety of local options including Panda Express, L&L Hawaiian Barbecue, and Goma Tei ramen. Budget ~$10–13.
meals.dinner: L&L Hawaiian Barbecue — plate lunches with rice and macaroni salad. Chicken katsu or kalbi plate ~$11–14. A Hawaii institution.

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings at Ala Moana are lively and fun. The free hula show is a wonderful cultural experience for families. Check the mall website for exact show times.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the KCC Farmers Market at Kapiolani Community College (open Saturdays 7:30 AM–11:00 AM, free entry) — one of Oahu's best farmers markets with local produce, prepared foods, fresh fruit, and artisan goods. Sample local flavors like fresh coconut, tropical fruits, and homemade jams.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Lanikai Beach on the Windward Coast (~45 min from Waikiki by car or bus). Consistently rated one of the world's most beautiful beaches — powdery white sand, turquoise water, and views of the Mokulua Islands. Free and uncrowded compared to Waikiki.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Lanikai or nearby Kailua Beach Park, then head back to Waikiki. Saturday evening is lively — enjoy free street entertainment along Kalakaua Avenue.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the KCC Farmers Market — fresh fruit, acai bowls, and local pastries for ~$8–12.
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua — a beloved local deli with fresh sandwiches and salads ~$12–15.
meals.dinner: Teddy's Bigger Burgers in Waikiki — local burger chain, great quality for ~$12–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Lanikai Beach has very limited parking — arrive early or park at Kailua Beach Park and walk. No facilities at Lanikai itself, so bring water and snacks. The water is calm and ideal for young children.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided walk of historic Chinatown Honolulu — explore colorful lei shops, fresh fish markets, and local bakeries. Visit the Oahu Market (one of Hawaii's oldest markets) and browse the vibrant street art. Pick up affordable fresh flowers and local snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nuuanu Pali Lookout (~20 min from Waikiki by car or bus) — a dramatic mountain overlook with sweeping views of the Windward Coast. Entry is $7/car or free on foot/bus. The wind is famously strong — hold onto hats and small children! Then stop at Queen Emma Summer Palace nearby (~$10/adult, $1/child) for a glimpse into Hawaiian royal history.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Waikiki — take a sunset catamaran cruise (budget options from ~$35–45/person with Waikiki Beach Services) or simply enjoy a final sunset walk on the beach. Browse ABC Stores for affordable Hawaii souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Dim sum breakfast in Chinatown at Legend Seafood Restaurant — dumplings, bao, and rice rolls for ~$10–13 per person.
meals.lunch: Chinatown's Maunakea Marketplace food court — diverse local vendors with plates from $8–11.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last full dinner: Duke's Waikiki happy hour (4–6 PM) offers discounted appetizers and drinks with an iconic beachfront setting. Budget ~$20–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Stock up on souvenirs at Chinatown or ABC Stores — much cheaper than airport shops. Macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, and Hawaiian sea salt make great affordable gifts. Pack bags tonight to prepare for departure.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning final swim or walk on Waikiki Beach — enjoy one last sunrise over Diamond Head. Check out of accommodation and store luggage if needed. Take a final stroll along the beachfront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Honolulu International Airport (Daniel K. Inouye International Airport) — allow at least 2–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute gifts. Reflect on an incredible 10-day Hawaii adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii. If returning to Buena Park/Anaheim area, arrive back at SureStay Hotel or continue onward. Rest and recover from an amazing trip.

meals.breakfast: One final plate lunch or breakfast at a local spot near the hotel — try Eggs 'n Things in Waikiki for classic Hawaiian breakfast (~$14–18) as a farewell treat.
meals.lunch: Airport food court — Makai Market at the airport has local options including poke and plate lunches (~$13–16).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or grab food upon return to California (~$10–15).

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 10 days (per person): Accommodation ~$350–500 (budget hostel/Airbnb), Food ~$150–200, Activities ~$100–150, Transportation ~$80–120, Flights variable. Total estimated land budget: ~$680–970 per person excluding flights. Always carry cash — many local food trucks and small vendors are cash-only.

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.description: Explore the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore with a self-guided food tour sampling legendary shave ice at Matsumoto's, fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and tropical fruit smoothies. Best enjoyed in the cooler morning or early evening hours while browsing local shops and galleries.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii airport at 11:20 AM via Alaska Airlines. Collect luggage, pick up rental car or arrange shuttle transfer to hotel. Check in early if possible or store luggage at the SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll to a nearby beach to get your first taste of Hawaii. Enjoy the ocean views, dip your toes in the water, and let the family decompress from travel. Visit a local ABC Store or Times Supermarket to stock up on snacks and essentials for the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Easy, relaxed first dinner close to the hotel. Explore the immediate neighborhood and find a casual local restaurant. Get to bed early to recover from travel and prepare for the adventures ahead.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport upon arrival — try a plate lunch from an airport food court vendor for a first taste of local flavors.
meals.lunch: Pick up poke bowls or a quick bite from a nearby grocery store deli or local poke shop (~$12–18 per person).
meals.dinner: Casual sit-down dinner at a family-friendly local restaurant near the hotel. Try a Hawaiian BBQ spot or a diner offering plate lunches with rice, macaroni salad, and grilled meats (~$15–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Since arrival is at 11:20 AM, keep Day 1 light and stress-free. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. Pick up a printed or downloaded map of the island to plan routes. Weather in August averages around 16.8°C with some rain — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Head out early to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for a family snorkeling adventure. Arrive by 7:00–8:00 AM to beat the crowds and secure parking (the bay often reaches capacity by mid-morning). Watch the mandatory marine education video, then snorkel in the calm, protected waters teeming with colorful tropical fish and sea turtles.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive along the scenic Kalanianaole Highway to Makapuu Point Lookout for stunning coastal views. Stop at Waimanalo Beach — one of Oahu's most beautiful and family-friendly beaches — for a relaxed afternoon swim and beach play.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Waikiki and enjoy the lively atmosphere. Walk along Kalakaua Avenue and browse the shops. Watch the free hula and live music performances at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (free nightly shows).

meals.breakfast: Eat before leaving the hotel — grab pastries and coffee from a nearby café or hotel breakfast (~$8–12 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy at Waimanalo Beach, or grab plate lunches from a nearby roadside lunch truck (~$10–15 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Waikiki at a mid-range restaurant. Try Marukame Udon for affordable, delicious udon noodles, or Eggs 'n Things for a fun family meal (~$15–22 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations online — book at least 2–3 days ahead. Entry fee is approximately $25 per adult; children under 13 are free. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, snorkel gear (rentable on-site), and water shoes. The bay is closed on Tuesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit. The trail opens at 6:00 AM — aim to start by 6:30 AM to catch the morning light and avoid midday heat. The 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside the volcanic crater is manageable for families with older children and rewards hikers with panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, head to Waikiki Beach for a relaxed afternoon. Rent boogie boards or try a beginner surf lesson with one of the many beachside surf schools. The gentle waves of Waikiki are perfect for first-timers and kids.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the International Market Place in Waikiki — a beautiful open-air shopping center with a great food hall. Browse local vendors and enjoy the lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a light breakfast before the hike — granola bars, fruit, and water from the hotel or a nearby convenience store.
meals.lunch: Post-hike brunch or lunch at Waikiki. Try Heavenly Island Lifestyle for healthy, locally sourced bowls and sandwiches (~$14–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the International Market Place food hall — choose from a variety of cuisines including Hawaiian, Japanese, and American options (~$15–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head State Monument charges a $5 per person entry fee (or $10 per vehicle). Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and wear comfortable closed-toe shoes. The hike includes stairs and a tunnel — not recommended for very young toddlers. Tuesday is a great day since Hanauma Bay is closed and crowds shift elsewhere.

day_by_day.morning: Drive up to Oahu's North Shore — about a 45–60 minute drive from Waikiki. Start with the Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa Town. Explore the charming surf town, visit Matsumoto Shave Ice (a legendary local institution), browse surf shops, and soak in the laid-back North Shore vibe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waimea Bay Beach Park for a beautiful afternoon swim. In summer, the waters are calm and ideal for families. Alternatively, visit Shark's Cove at Pupukea for excellent snorkeling in tide pools — great for kids to explore marine life up close.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Honolulu along the scenic Kamehameha Highway. Stop at a roadside shrimp truck near Kahuku for a classic North Shore experience before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or grab a smoothie and acai bowl from a café in Haleiwa (~$10–14 per person).
meals.lunch: Self-guided food tour in Haleiwa — sample local favorites including shave ice, garlic shrimp, and fresh fruit from roadside stands (~$15–20 per person total).
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck or Romy's Kahuku Prawns near Kahuku for the famous North Shore garlic shrimp plate (~$14–18 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is about 35 miles from Waikiki — plan for traffic, especially on weekends. In August, North Shore waves are small and calm (big wave season is winter). Bring cash for shrimp trucks and small vendors. Shark's Cove is best explored at low tide.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day experience at the Polynesian Cultural Center in Laie on Oahu's North Shore. Arrive when it opens (around 11:45 AM for the standard package, or earlier for premium packages). Explore six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire-making, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — enjoy canoe rides on the lagoon, watch live cultural demonstrations, and let the kids interact with performers. The center is designed for families and offers activities for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the spectacular 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show — a world-class Polynesian theatrical performance with fire dancing, drumming, and stunning choreography. This is a highlight of any Hawaii family trip.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel before the drive to Laie (~$10–15 per person at a nearby café).
meals.lunch: Ali'i Luau buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included in some packages, or available as an add-on. Features traditional Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes (~$45–55 per adult, less for children).
meals.dinner: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center (included with evening show packages) or grab a meal at a nearby restaurant in Laie (~$20–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets in advance online — packages range from ~$60–120+ per adult depending on inclusions. The 'Ali'i Luau + Ha Show' combo package offers the best value for families. The center is run by Brigham Young University–Hawaii and is alcohol-free. Allow a full day — the center is about 35 miles from Waikiki.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning visit to Pearl Harbor — one of Hawaii's most significant historical sites. Visit the USS Arizona Memorial (free, but timed passes required — book in advance at recreation.gov), the Battleship Missouri, and the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum. This is an educational and moving experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Pearl Harbor, head to Aloha Tower Marketplace in downtown Honolulu for lunch and a stroll along the historic waterfront. Browse local shops and enjoy the harbor views. Visit the nearby Chinatown district for a cultural walkthrough and unique local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a sunset walk along the beach and watch the famous Waikiki sunset. Browse the Waikiki Beach Walk outdoor shopping area.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near the hotel before heading to Pearl Harbor — try a local diner or café (~$10–14 per person).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Aloha Tower Marketplace — try Gordon Biersch Brewery Restaurant for burgers and local fare, or grab casual bites from the food vendors (~$15–22 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Waikiki at Duke's Waikiki — a beloved beachfront restaurant with Hawaiian-inspired dishes and ocean views (~$25–40 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor USS Arizona Memorial boat tours are free but require advance timed-entry reservations at recreation.gov — book weeks ahead as they fill up fast. The Battleship Missouri and Aviation Museum have separate admission fees (~$30–35 per adult). Allow 3–4 hours for Pearl Harbor. Dress respectfully — no swimwear.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Maui Ocean Center Aquarium — Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring a stunning walk-through underwater tunnel, Hawaiian green sea turtles, manta rays, and hundreds of marine species. This is a fantastic family activity, especially if weather is overcast. Note: This requires a short inter-island flight or ferry to Maui — plan accordingly, or substitute with the Waikiki Aquarium on Oahu if staying on-island.
day_by_day.afternoon: If on Maui: Explore the charming town of Lahaina — browse art galleries, historic sites, and the famous Banyan Tree Park. Walk along Front Street for shopping and ocean views. If staying on Oahu: Visit Kailua Beach on the windward coast — consistently rated one of Hawaii's best beaches, with calm turquoise waters and white sand perfect for families.
day_by_day.evening: If on Maui: Enjoy a sunset dinner in Lahaina. If on Oahu: Return to Waikiki and enjoy a relaxed evening with a beachside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café before heading out (~$10–14 per person).
meals.lunch: If at Maui Ocean Center: Seascape Ma'alaea Restaurant inside the aquarium offers casual dining with ocean views (~$15–22 per person). If on Oahu: Grab lunch at a Kailua café like Cinnamon's Restaurant (~$14–20 per person).
meals.dinner: If on Maui: Lahaina Grill or Kimo's Restaurant for fresh seafood and Hawaiian cuisine (~$30–45 per person). If on Oahu: Buzz's Original Steakhouse in Kailua for a classic local experience (~$25–40 per person).

day_by_day.notes: If visiting Maui Ocean Center, book a same-day return inter-island flight (Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest) — flights are about 30 minutes and can be affordable if booked in advance. Alternatively, treat Day 7 as a full Oahu beach day at Kailua or Lanikai Beach to keep things simple and budget-friendly. Maui Ocean Center admission is ~$35 per adult, ~$25 per child.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Explore exhibits on Hawaiian royalty, ancient artifacts, natural history, and the Pacific. The planetarium show is a hit with kids. This is a great option for a potentially rainy morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ala Moana Beach Park — a beautiful, family-friendly beach adjacent to the famous Ala Moana Center. Enjoy swimming in the calm, protected waters, build sandcastles, and relax on the wide sandy beach. The park has excellent facilities including restrooms, picnic areas, and lifeguards.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ala Moana Center — one of the world's largest open-air shopping malls — for dinner and evening shopping. Catch the free hula show performed at the Centerstage on select evenings.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near the hotel — try Liliha Bakery for famous coco puffs and local breakfast plates (~$10–15 per person).
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Ala Moana Beach Park — pick up supplies from Foodland Farms supermarket nearby, or grab plate lunches from a local takeout spot (~$10–15 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ala Moana Center — try Mariposa at Neiman Marcus for a splurge, or opt for the food court with diverse affordable options (~$15–30 per person depending on choice).

day_by_day.notes: Bishop Museum admission is ~$25 per adult, ~$17 per child. Check the museum's schedule for special programs and planetarium show times. Ala Moana Beach Park is free and has excellent facilities — arrive early on weekends as it gets busy. The hula show at Ala Moana Center is free and typically held on Fridays and Sundays — check the current schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Take a scenic drive around the entire Oahu coastline — the Circle Island Tour. Start by heading east along the H-1 to the Pali Highway, stopping at the Nu'uanu Pali Lookout for breathtaking views of the windward coast and the dramatic Ko'olau Mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the circle island drive north through Kaneohe and Kualoa Ranch area. Stop at Kualoa Regional Park for a beautiful beach break with views of the Mokoli'i (Chinaman's Hat) island. Continue to the North Shore for one last visit, stopping at Sunset Beach and Ehukai Beach Park (Banzai Pipeline) to see the famous surf spots.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a final evening on the island. Enjoy a sunset cruise or simply watch the sunset from the beach. Have a special farewell dinner to celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café before the drive (~$10–14 per person).
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside lunch truck or local plate lunch spot along the North Shore — try Ted's Bakery near Sunset Beach for famous cream pies and plate lunches (~$12–18 per person).
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a Waikiki restaurant with ocean views — try Hula Grill Waikiki or Orchids at Halekulani for a memorable mid-range splurge (~$35–55 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The full circle island drive is approximately 100 miles and takes 4–6 hours with stops — start early. Nu'uanu Pali Lookout can be windy — bring a light jacket. Kualoa Ranch also offers ATV tours, movie site tours (Jurassic Park was filmed here), and horseback riding if the family wants to add an activity (~$50–120 per person per activity, book in advance).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and take one last walk on the beach. Pack up and check out of the hotel. If time allows before departure, visit the Waikiki Aquarium (a smaller, affordable alternative to Maui Ocean Center) or browse the Waikiki Farmers Market for local souvenirs, macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, and Hawaiian honey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport for departure. Allow extra time for car rental return and airport check-in. Browse the airport's local shops for last-minute souvenirs — Honolulu Airport has excellent local vendors including Leis by the Yard and local food options.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Hawaii — carry wonderful memories of beaches, culture, and family adventures.

meals.breakfast: Final Hawaiian breakfast — try a local spot for one last acai bowl, loco moco (rice, hamburger patty, fried egg, and gravy), or fresh tropical fruit plate (~$12–18 per person).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick bite near the hotel before heading to the airport — grab a poke bowl or plate lunch to go (~$12–16 per person).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or dinner at the destination airport upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time and plan hotel checkout accordingly — most hotels allow checkout until 11:00 AM (request late checkout if needed). Return rental car with a full tank to avoid extra fees. Honolulu Airport (HNL) recommends arriving 2–3 hours before international or mainland flights. Pack any fresh fruit or agricultural products carefully — Hawaii has strict agricultural export rules and TSA may inspect items.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
experiences.description: A family-friendly snorkeling adventure in a protected marine sanctuary teeming with colorful fish and sea turtles. Arrive early to secure entry and enjoy calm, clear waters before crowds build. An indoor education center provides a great rainy-day or midday alternative with marine life exhibits.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Experience
experiences.description: An immersive family cultural experience featuring six Polynesian villages, live performances, canoe rides, and traditional craft demonstrations. The indoor evening luau and IMAX theater make it a perfect option to avoid midday heat while learning about Hawaiian and Pacific Island heritage.

experiences.name: Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit
experiences.description: A manageable 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside a volcanic crater offering panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Best tackled at sunrise to beat the heat and crowds. Kids ages 5 and up can typically complete this trail, making it a memorable family achievement.

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium Visit
experiences.description: Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring a walk-through underwater tunnel, Hawaiian green sea turtles, manta rays, and interactive tide pools. This is an ideal indoor midday or rainy-day activity for families, offering hours of educational entertainment while staying cool and sheltered.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa Town
experiences.description: Explore the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore with a self-guided food tour sampling legendary shave ice at Matsumoto's, fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and tropical fruit smoothies. Best enjoyed in the cooler morning or early evening hours while browsing local shops and galleries.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii — Flight Alaska lands at 11:20 AM. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to the SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll along the nearest beach or hotel pool area to decompress from travel. Visit a nearby luxury spa for a welcome massage or relaxation treatment to reset after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at a premium local restaurant near the hotel. Explore the Buena Park area with a gentle evening walk or lounge at the hotel bar with tropical cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Light snack or meal on the flight before landing
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the hotel restaurant or a nearby upscale café — try fresh Hawaiian-style poke bowls or a gourmet sandwich
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium steakhouse or seafood restaurant near Buena Park — recommend a place with fresh Pacific seafood and a curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 11:20 AM arrival. Focus on rest and acclimatization. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings and arrange private transportation for the days ahead. Pack reef-safe sunscreen for beach activities.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit — a manageable 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside a volcanic crater offering breathtaking panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Depart by 6:00 AM to catch the sunrise and beat the crowds. Hire a private guide for an enriched experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for a world-class snorkeling adventure in a protected marine sanctuary. Enjoy the colorful reef fish, sea turtles, and crystal-clear waters. Reserve premium snorkel gear rentals in advance. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the bay.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel, freshen up, and enjoy a sunset cocktail hour at a rooftop bar or beachfront lounge. Dine at a fine dining restaurant featuring Hawaiian fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike light breakfast at the hotel — fresh fruit, granola, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the hotel or a premium deli near Hanauma Bay — fresh sandwiches, tropical fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Upscale Hawaiian fusion dinner at a restaurant like a Waikiki fine dining venue — fresh catch of the day, taro-crusted preparations, and local desserts

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations and charges an entry fee. Arrive early as capacity is limited. Wear reef-safe sunscreen only — chemical sunscreens are banned at the preserve. The Diamond Head hike is best done before 8:00 AM to avoid heat and crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center for an immersive family cultural experience. Explore six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa, Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Participate in hands-on cultural activities including fire-making, weaving, and canoe rides. Book the premium Ambassador package for VIP access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — enjoy the IMAX film 'Hā: Breath of Life' and participate in afternoon village demonstrations. Take a guided canoe journey along the lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the spectacular 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a world-class Polynesian performance with fire dancing, drumming, and storytelling. Enjoy the included premium luau dinner with the Ambassador package.

meals.breakfast: Full American breakfast at the hotel before departing — eggs, fresh tropical fruit, pastries, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Included in the Polynesian Cultural Center Ambassador package — traditional Polynesian buffet with kalua pork, poi, fresh fish, and tropical desserts
meals.dinner: Premium luau dinner included with the evening show package — traditional Hawaiian feast with imu-roasted pig, lomi salmon, haupia, and fresh pineapple

day_by_day.notes: Book the Polynesian Cultural Center Ambassador VIP package well in advance as it sells out quickly. The package includes priority seating, a guided tour, and premium dining. Allow a full day for this experience — it is approximately 45 minutes from Waikiki. Arrange private round-trip transportation.

day_by_day.morning: Depart for Oahu's North Shore — visit the legendary surf town of Haleiwa for the Shave Ice and Local Food Tour. Begin with a self-guided gourmet food tour sampling Matsumoto's world-famous shave ice, fresh acai bowls, garlic shrimp from a premium food truck, and local artisan treats. Explore the charming boutiques and galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a premium North Shore beach such as Waimea Bay or Sunset Beach for an afternoon of relaxation and swimming. In August, the waters are calm and ideal for families. Arrange a private surfing lesson or stand-up paddleboard session with a certified instructor.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the hotel area and stop at a premium farm-to-table restaurant on the way. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a sunset view and locally sourced Hawaiian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel — fresh smoothie bowls, toast, and Kona coffee before the early departure
meals.lunch: North Shore food tour experience — shave ice, garlic shrimp plates, fresh poke, and tropical fruit from Haleiwa's best vendors
meals.dinner: Farm-to-table dinner at a premium restaurant featuring locally grown produce, fresh-caught fish, and Hawaiian craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is approximately 1 hour from Waikiki — arrange a private driver for the day for comfort and flexibility. August is the calm season on the North Shore, making it perfect for swimming and water activities. Bring cash for some of the local food vendors in Haleiwa.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a premium private catamaran sailing tour along the Oahu coastline. Depart from Waikiki or Kewalo Basin for a morning sail with snorkeling stops, dolphin watching, and stunning coastal views. Many luxury charters include continental breakfast and champagne on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pearl Harbor and the USS Arizona Memorial for a historically significant and moving experience. Book a premium guided tour for in-depth historical context. Explore the Battleship Missouri and the Pacific Aviation Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a premium spa treatment at a luxury spa near the hotel, followed by a sophisticated dinner at a fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast and champagne served on the private catamaran during the morning sail
meals.lunch: Upscale lunch near Pearl Harbor — a premium café or restaurant with fresh Hawaiian cuisine and ocean views
meals.dinner: Elegant dinner at a top-rated fine dining restaurant — omakase sushi, fresh Hawaiian seafood, or a premium tasting menu with wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor requires advance reservations, especially for the USS Arizona Memorial boat tour. The memorial is free but timed entry passes must be booked online. The private catamaran charter should be booked at least 2 weeks in advance. Dress respectfully for the Pearl Harbor visit.

day_by_day.morning: Take a premium helicopter tour over Oahu for breathtaking aerial views of Diamond Head, the Ko'olau Mountains, the North Shore, and the stunning coastline. Many luxury operators offer doors-off experiences for photography enthusiasts. This is a bucket-list experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Maui Ocean Center Aquarium — Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring a walk-through underwater tunnel, Hawaiian green sea turtles, manta rays, and fascinating marine exhibits. Book a behind-the-scenes VIP tour for an exclusive experience. Note: If on Oahu, visit the Waikiki Aquarium as an alternative.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium sunset dinner cruise along the Waikiki coastline. Many luxury operators offer fine dining, live Hawaiian music, and open bar packages while watching the sun set over the Pacific.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the hotel before the helicopter tour — eggs Benedict, fresh tropical fruit, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the aquarium — fresh poke bowls, sushi, or a premium café with ocean views
meals.dinner: Premium sunset dinner cruise — multi-course dinner with fresh seafood, Hawaiian entertainment, and open bar

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours should be booked well in advance and are weather-dependent. Weight restrictions apply for helicopter tours — confirm with the operator. The Maui Ocean Center is technically on Maui; if remaining on Oahu, substitute with the Waikiki Aquarium or Sea Life Park for a family-friendly marine experience.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely morning at a premium Waikiki beach club with reserved loungers, umbrella service, and beach butler. Swim in the calm August waters, try a beginner surfing lesson with a private instructor, or simply relax with a tropical drink in hand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's premier luxury shopping destination featuring high-end brands, local designers, and gourmet food options. Pick up premium Hawaiian souvenirs, macadamia nut products, and local artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Hawaiian luau at a premium venue such as the Royal Hawaiian Hotel's Azure Luau or a comparable luxury luau experience. Enjoy traditional hula performances, fire dancing, and a lavish feast.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely brunch at a beachfront restaurant — avocado toast, fresh tropical fruit, eggs, and mimosas
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at Ala Moana Center's premium food hall or a nearby upscale restaurant — fresh sushi, Hawaiian plate lunch elevated, or a premium burger
meals.dinner: Traditional Hawaiian luau feast — kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, fresh fish, tropical desserts, and mai tais

day_by_day.notes: Reserve beach club loungers and the luau experience in advance. The Royal Hawaiian Hotel's Azure Luau is one of the most prestigious in Oahu and books out weeks ahead. August weather is warm and sunny — stay hydrated and apply sunscreen regularly throughout the beach day.

day_by_day.morning: Take a premium guided kayaking or outrigger canoe tour along the Waikiki coastline or toward the Mokulua Islands. This is a wonderful family activity with calm August waters. A private guide will share Hawaiian cultural stories and point out marine life along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Explore the Hawaiian Hall, planetarium, and Science Adventure Center. Book a private guided tour for a deeper understanding of Hawaiian history, mythology, and natural science.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium private chef dinner experience — arrange for a top local chef to prepare a multi-course Hawaiian tasting menu at a private venue or luxury villa setting. This is an extraordinary culinary experience for the family.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel — fresh fruit, yogurt, granola, and coffee before the kayaking tour
meals.lunch: Post-museum lunch at a premium restaurant near the Bishop Museum — fresh Hawaiian cuisine with local ingredients
meals.dinner: Private chef multi-course tasting dinner — Hawaiian ingredients elevated with fine dining techniques, paired with local wines and craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Outrigger canoe tours are a deeply cultural Hawaiian experience — choose an operator that employs Native Hawaiian guides for an authentic experience. The private chef dinner should be arranged at least 5–7 days in advance through a luxury concierge service. This is an ideal evening for a special family memory.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a premium whale watching and marine wildlife tour (note: humpback whales are typically in Hawaii from December–May, but August offers excellent dolphin, sea turtle, and tropical fish encounters). Book a luxury small-group boat tour for an intimate ocean experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kailua Beach — consistently rated one of Hawaii's most beautiful beaches. Enjoy the powdery white sand, turquoise waters, and calm conditions perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Rent premium paddleboards or kayaks for exploring the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Hawaii — celebrate with a premium farewell dinner at one of Oahu's most acclaimed fine dining restaurants. Choose a venue with panoramic ocean views and a menu showcasing the best of Hawaiian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel — full spread with eggs, fresh tropical fruit, pastries, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside picnic at Kailua Beach — premium gourmet picnic basket arranged by the hotel with fresh sandwiches, fruit, sparkling water, and local treats
meals.dinner: Farewell fine dining dinner — premium tasting menu with wine pairings at a top-rated Oahu restaurant with ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach is approximately 30–40 minutes from Waikiki — arrange private transportation. The beach has limited parking so a private driver is recommended. For the farewell dinner, make reservations at least 1–2 weeks in advance at a top-rated venue. Consider a restaurant on a high floor or rooftop for panoramic sunset views.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a last peaceful walk along the beach or hotel grounds to soak in the Hawaiian atmosphere. Do any final souvenir shopping or pick up premium local products such as Kona coffee, macadamia nuts, Hawaiian sea salt, and local honey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and transfer via private luxury car service to the airport. Allow ample time for check-in and security. Browse the premium shops at the airport for any last-minute gifts or Hawaiian treats.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with wonderful memories of a premium family vacation. Enjoy the flight home with premium class seating and reflect on 10 incredible days in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full gourmet breakfast at the hotel — enjoy every last bite of fresh Hawaiian tropical fruit, eggs, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or a nearby café before airport transfer — fresh poke bowl or a premium sandwich
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or a meal at the airport's premium lounge before departure

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — arrange a late checkout if possible to maximize your final morning. Confirm private airport transfer the night before. Ensure all premium souvenirs and food items comply with TSA and agricultural regulations — fresh fruits and certain plant products cannot be taken off the islands. Pack any liquid items such as honey or sauces in checked luggage.
